subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
passage: The colony picnic at the park had been rained off, so the families gathered in the community hall instead. Harsha's father, Omkar, spread a mat, his mother unpacked sandwiches, and a board game came out of a bag. Harsha dragged a chair to the wall and folded his arms. "Everything is spoiled," he said. His little sister held up the dice. "No." Around the mat, the games got louder and someone started a song. Harsha watched from his chair, chewing a cold sandwich, hearing every laugh. When it was time to go home, he realised he had spent the whole cosy afternoon looking at it from across the room.

qa.q: Where did the families gather after the picnic was rained off?
qa.a: The families gathered in the community hall.

qa.q: What was Harsha feeling as he sat by the wall, and how does his behaviour show it?
qa.a: Angry and disappointed, since he folded his arms, said everything was spoiled and refused the game.

qa.q: What could Harsha have done instead of sulking, and why?
qa.a: He could have joined the board game and treated it as a different kind of picnic, because the day was still there to enjoy.

qa.q: How might Harsha's father feel seeing him sit apart?
qa.a: Probably sad and a little helpless, since Omkar had spread the mat to make the day cosy and Harsha would not join.

grounding: A boy whose picnic is rained off sulks and blames, and misses the cosy day the family arranged.

subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
passage: I'm Vandana, Jatin's aunt, and I'd come over for the picnic that never happened. When the rain started at nine, Jatin threw himself on the sofa and said, "Everything's spoiled. Everything." His mother spread the picnic sheet on the living-room floor and set out the aloo sandwiches. Jatin didn't move. His father put on the old songs and started a card game with the little ones. Jatin said, "This isn't a picnic." We made chai and hot pakoras, and everyone sat on the sheet laughing when the baby tried to eat a card. Jatin stayed on the sofa with his arms folded all afternoon. In the evening he asked if there were any pakoras left. There weren't. I don't know if he was angry at the rain or at us.

qa.q: What did Jatin's mother spread on the floor?
What might Jatin have been feeling on the sofa?
qa.a: Angry and disappointed that the picnic was spoiled.

qa.q: What else could Jatin have done?
qa.a: Joined the indoor picnic and asked to plan the real one for another weekend.

qa.q: How does Vandana see Jatin's afternoon?
qa.a: Vandana sees him miss the fun and the pakoras, but doesn't know whether he was angry at the rain or at the family.

grounding: An aunt watches a boy sulk all afternoon when rain spoils a picnic, missing the cosy indoor day the family arranges.

subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
passage:
Saturday: The lake picnic Hemant had waited for all month was cancelled when the rain began at seven. He stomped to his room. "It's all ruined. I hate rain."
Sunday: It was still pouring. From his room he could hear his brother Anirban and their parents building a blanket tent in the hall, and smell khichdi and papad. Anirban knocked. "We're doing a torch picnic inside. Come." "It's stupid," Hemant said through the door.
Monday: At school, Anirban told his friends about the blanket tent and the ghost stories by torchlight. Hemant listened, saying nothing. That evening he asked his mother, "Can we do the tent again?" "Maybe next rainy day," she said.

qa.q: What were Anirban and their parents building?
qa.a: A blanket tent in the hall.

qa.q: What might Hemant have felt listening to Anirban on Monday?
qa.a: Left out and regretful that he had missed the fun by sulking.

qa.q: What else could Hemant have done on Sunday?
qa.a: Joined the torch picnic, and asked separately to reschedule the lake trip.

qa.q: How did the rainy weekend feel for Anirban?
qa.a: Anirban enjoyed the tent and ghost stories and happily told his friends about them.

grounding: Over three days, a boy who sulks about a rained-off picnic misses the cosy day his family makes of it.
